ma_sunbowl.blurb: Sunbowl is a short sport crag in Sunderland, Western Massachusetts, standing about 35 feet tall. Nineteen bolted lines run from 5.6 up to 5.11, with the biggest group at 5.10, so it suits newer leaders stepping up as well as anyone wanting a quick session. The conglomerate is pocketed and cobbled, with slabby sections on either side of a steeper central face and a short low traverse along the base. It faces southwest, takes the sun from around midday and stays pleasant through the cooler months, while the tree canopy cools it in summer. The top is awkward to reach, so most parties lead a line and then hang a rope.
ma_sunbowl.parking_note: Reach Reservoir Road by way of North Silver Lane off Route 116, then drive it to the end of the paved section and leave the car near the water tower.
ma_sunbowl.approach: Walk a short way up the road, then follow an ATV track into the woods, crossing a stream and climbing the slope. Keep left where the track splits and pass small cliffs, then at a cairn on the high ground turn right onto a footpath and follow the cairns until the crag shows on your left.

ma_3_wizard_s_cave.blurb: Wizard's Cave is a group of eighteen boulder problems inside Rock House Reservation, a wooded reserve on the Ware and West Brookfield line in central Massachusetts. Most lines fall between V0 and V4, which makes it a friendly spot for newer boulderers, with a single V5 above that and two very hard problems at the top end. The reservation is scattered with glacial blocks and is busy with local families in summer, so expect company. Some problems may want a brushing before you pull on, and sun and shade are not well described, so be ready for damp or mossy holds.

ma_chumbo_farmstrong_area.blurb: Chumbo/Farmstrong is the broad boulderfield that spreads out beneath the Overhang Buttress and the Amphitheater at Rose Ledge in western Massachusetts. All seventeen problems are boulders, and the spread is wide: a cluster around V2, a few in the V3 to V5 range, and then a steep jump, with nearly half of them V7 or harder and the top line reaching V12. That makes it a better stop for strong boulderers than for beginners. Rose Ledge as a whole mixes roofs, slabs and tall lines, with most problems sitting just under the cliff line.

ma_oz.blurb: Oz is a small crag at Redrocks on Cape Ann, only about 30 feet high but full of slab and crack climbing. Of its seventeen climbs, ten are trad, four are sport, one is a top rope and two are short boulder problems along the top. Most lines sit between 5.6 and 5.9, with a couple of 5.10 and 5.11 climbs for variety. The granite is shaded and dries fairly quickly, and it makes a handy alternative when the main Redrocks wall is crowded. Many route names follow a Wizard of Oz theme.
ma_oz.parking_note: Leave the car in the main Redrocks lot beside Route 128, on the north side of the Route 133 overpass just short of the storage units.
ma_oz.approach: Follow the main trail along Route 128 past the storage units, then turn north up the pipeline trail. Climb about 100 yards until the crag appears among the trees on your left. The whole walk is roughly a third of a mile.
